title: MAP Sensor Circuit Low Input
problem: The Manifold Absolute Pressure sensor voltage is below the minimum expected range.
symptoms: Rich running; Poor throttle response; Engine stalling; Black smoke from exhaust
actions: Check MAP sensor connector for corrosion; Inspect vacuum hose for leaks; Test sensor voltage (should be 0.5–4.5V); Replace MAP sensor if faulty
location: Intake manifold or throttle body area.

title: MAP Sensor Circuit High Input
problem: The Manifold Absolute Pressure sensor voltage is above the maximum expected range.
symptoms: Lean mixture; Hesitation on acceleration; Rough idle; High fuel consumption
actions: Check MAP sensor wiring for shorts to power; Verify 5V reference voltage at sensor; Test sensor resistance; Replace MAP sensor
location: Intake manifold or throttle body area.

title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
problem: The ECT sensor signal is below the expected minimum voltage
symptoms: indicating a possible short to ground or failed sensor.
actions: Temperature gauge reads max/hot; Engine runs rich; Poor fuel economy; Fan runs constantly
location: Check ECT sensor connector and wiring; Test sensor resistance (cold ~10kΩ
column10: hot ~150Ω); Inspect for water ingress in connector; Replace ECT sensor

title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor Circuit High
problem: The ECT sensor signal is above the expected maximum voltage
symptoms: indicating open circuit or failed sensor.
actions: Temperature gauge reads cold/zero; Engine runs rich on startup; Poor fuel economy; Cooling fan won't turn on
location: Check ECT sensor wiring for open circuit; Test sensor with multimeter; Check connector pins for corrosion; Replace ECT sensor

title: Throttle Position Sensor Signal Low
problem: The voltage signal from Throttle Position Sensor 'A' is lower than the expected range.
symptoms: Poor acceleration; Stalling at idle; Jerking while riding; Hesitation on throttle
actions: Check TPS connector for corrosion; Verify 5V reference voltage at TPS; Adjust TPS to correct angle; Replace TPS if out of spec
location: Mounted on the side of the throttle body.

title: Throttle Position Sensor Signal High
problem: The voltage signal from Throttle Position Sensor 'A' is higher than the expected range.
symptoms: High idle speed; Jerky acceleration; Engine surging; Poor fuel economy
actions: Check TPS wiring for short to power; Test TPS voltage at wide-open throttle (should be ~4.5V); Adjust TPS mounting position; Replace TPS
location: Mounted on the side of the throttle body.

title: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
problem: The oxygen sensor is consistently reading a lean mixture or the sensor signal voltage is too low.
symptoms: Poor fuel economy; Rough idle; Check engine light; Possible black smoke or lean surge
actions: Check O2 sensor wiring harness; Inspect for exhaust leaks near sensor; Test sensor voltage (should vary 0.1–0.9V); Replace O2 sensor if >100
location: 000 km
column10: On the exhaust pipe, before the catalytic converter.

title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
problem: The oxygen sensor is consistently reading a rich mixture or the sensor signal is stuck high.
symptoms: Rich running; Black exhaust smoke; Fuel smell; Poor fuel economy
actions: Check for fuel injector leaking/stuck open; Inspect O2 sensor for contamination (oil or coolant); Test sensor at operating temperature; Replace O2 sensor
location: On the exhaust pipe, before the catalytic converter.

title: System Too Lean (Bank 1)
problem: The ECU is adding more fuel than normal (positive fuel trim) to compensate for a lean condition.
symptoms: Lean surge at steady throttle; Hesitation on acceleration; Rough idle; Engine stalling
actions: Check for air leaks in intake system; Inspect fuel pressure; Clean fuel injector; Check MAP/MAF sensor; Inspect for vacuum leaks
location: Intake manifold, fuel rail, injectors.

title: System Too Rich (Bank 1)
problem: The ECU is reducing fuel delivery (negative fuel trim) to compensate for an overly rich mixture.
symptoms: Black exhaust smoke; Strong fuel smell; Poor fuel economy; Engine flooding
actions: Check fuel pressure regulator; Inspect injector for leaking; Check O2 sensor operation; Inspect MAP sensor for fault; Check air filter – may be blocked
location: Fuel rail, injectors, intake.

title: Cylinder 1 Injector Circuit Low
problem: The ECU detected low voltage or a short to ground in the fuel injector circuit for cylinder 1.
symptoms: Engine misfire on cylinder 1; Loss of power; Strong fuel smell; Rough idle
actions: Check injector wiring harness for damage; Test injector resistance (typically 11–16 Ω); Check ECU injector driver output; Clean or replace fuel injector
location: Attached to the intake manifold, spraying into the cylinder head.

title: Cylinder 1 Injector Circuit High
problem: The ECU detected high voltage or open circuit in the fuel injector circuit for cylinder 1.
symptoms: Engine misfire; Hard starting; Engine runs on fewer cylinders
actions: Check injector connector and pins; Test injector coil resistance; Inspect wiring for open circuit; Replace injector if open coil
location: Attached to the intake manifold.

title: Random / Multiple Cylinder Misfire
problem: The ECU has detected misfires in multiple or random cylinders
symptoms: indicating a general ignition or fuel system problem.
actions: Rough idle; Vibration; Loss of power; Check engine light flashing; Backfiring
location: Check spark plugs – replace if worn; Inspect ignition coil(s); Check fuel pressure; Inspect injectors; Check compression

title: Cylinder 1 Misfire Detected
problem: The ECU has detected a misfire on cylinder 1 specifically.
symptoms: Rough idle at low RPM; Loss of power on cylinder 1; Backfiring; Increased emissions
actions: Replace spark plug on cylinder 1; Test ignition coil for cylinder 1; Check fuel injector on cylinder 1; Perform compression test on cylinder 1
location: Cylinder head, cylinder 1.

title: Crankshaft Position Sensor 'A' Circuit
problem: The ECU is not receiving a valid signal from the crankshaft position sensor.
symptoms: Engine won't start; Engine stalls unexpectedly; Backfiring; No spark
actions: Check CKP sensor air gap (typically 0.5–1.5 mm); Inspect sensor wiring harness for damage; Clean debris from sensor tip and reluctor ring; Replace CKP sensor
location: Near the crankshaft pulley or stator on the engine casing.

title: Crankshaft Position Sensor 'A' Range/Performance
problem: The CKP sensor signal is erratic or intermittent — detected but not within expected parameters.
symptoms: Hard starting; Stalling at idle; Erratic idle; Intermittent engine cut-out
actions: Check CKP sensor gap — too close or too far causes erratic signal; Inspect reluctor ring for damage or missing teeth; Check wiring for intermittent fault; Replace sensor
location: Near the crankshaft pulley or stator.

title: Camshaft Position Sensor 'A' Circuit
problem: The ECU is not receiving a signal from the camshaft position sensor.
symptoms: Engine won't start; Engine stalling; Timing-related misfires; Poor power
actions: Check CMP sensor wiring; Inspect sensor mounting and gap; Verify sensor target wheel condition; Replace CMP sensor
location: Near the cam sprocket or valve cover.

title: Camshaft Position Sensor 'A' Range/Performance
problem: The camshaft position sensor signal is erratic or out of expected range.
symptoms: Rough running; Poor timing; Hesitation; Intermittent stalling
actions: Check target wheel for debris or damage; Inspect sensor gap; Test sensor output with oscilloscope; Replace CMP sensor
location: Near the cam sprocket or valve cover.

title: System Voltage Low
problem: The electrical system voltage has dropped below the required threshold for normal ECU operation.
symptoms: Dim lights; Electrical systems cutting out; ECU resets; Battery warning light
actions: Test battery voltage (should be 12.6V+ at rest); Check charging system – test stator output; Inspect voltage regulator/rectifier; Check all ground connections; Replace battery if below 12V
location: Battery, stator, voltage regulator/rectifier.

title: System Voltage High
problem: The electrical system voltage is above the safe operating threshold
symptoms: indicating overcharging.
actions: Lights burning out frequently; Battery damage; Electronic component failures
location: Test voltage regulator output (should be 13.5–14.5V); Replace faulty voltage regulator/rectifier; Check stator windings; Test battery condition
column10: Usually mounted with fins for cooling

title: Vehicle Speed Sensor Malfunction
problem: The ECU is not receiving a valid signal from the vehicle speed sensor.
symptoms: Speedometer not working or erratic; ABS warning light; Poor idle control; Gear shift indicator not working
actions: Check speed sensor at rear wheel or gearbox output; Clean sensor tip and tone ring; Inspect wiring harness; Replace VSS if faulty
location: At the rear wheel hub or gearbox output shaft.

title: Idle Control System Malfunction
problem: The idle air control system is not maintaining the correct idle speed.
symptoms: High idle speed; Low/rough idle; Idle hunting (fluctuating); Stalling at stops
actions: Clean idle air control valve or stepper motor; Check throttle body for carbon deposits; Inspect idle speed bypass air circuit; Check TPS adjustment; Replace IAC valve if failed
location: On or near the throttle body.

title: Internal Control Module Memory Check Sum Error
problem: The ECU internal memory has failed a checksum test
symptoms: indicating possible memory corruption.
actions: Multiple random fault codes; Erratic engine behavior; Engine won't start; Loss of all settings
location: Try disconnecting battery for 15 minutes to reset; Reflash/remap ECU if possible; Replace ECU if fault persists; Contact dealer for ECU diagnosis
column10: Usually under the seat or in the fairing.

title: Malfunction Indicator Lamp (MIL) Control Circuit
problem: The circuit controlling the check engine light has a fault.
symptoms: Check engine light always on; Check engine light never comes on even with faults
actions: Check MIL bulb or LED condition; Inspect wiring from ECU to dashboard; Test ECU MIL output pin; Check instrument cluster ground
location: Dashboard instrument cluster.

title: Fuel Pump Primary Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECU is not receiving feedback that the fuel pump relay has activated correctly.
symptoms: Engine cranks but won't start; Engine stalls and won't restart; No fuel pump prime sound on ignition
actions: Listen for fuel pump prime (1–2 sec after ignition ON); Check fuel pump relay; Test fuel pump fuse; Measure fuel pressure; Replace fuel pump if no pressure
location: Fuel tank (pump inside) and relay near ECU.

title: Ignition Coil 'A' Primary/Secondary Circuit
problem: Fault detected in the ignition coil circuit – could be primary (driver) or secondary (HT) side.
symptoms: No spark; Misfire; Engine won't start; Backfiring through exhaust
actions: Check ignition coil primary resistance (typically 0.5–3 Ω); Check secondary resistance (typically 7–15 kΩ); Inspect HT lead and spark plug cap resistance; Replace ignition coil if out of spec
location: Mounted near or on the cylinder head.

title: Evaporative Emission Control System Purge Control Valve Circuit
problem: The EVAP purge control valve or its circuit has a fault.
symptoms: Fuel smell; Rough idle; Check engine light
actions: Check EVAP purge valve solenoid wiring; Test valve for operation (12V power should open it); Check for cracked or disconnected vacuum hoses; Replace purge valve if failed
location: On the intake manifold or near the fuel tank.

title: Control Module Power Supply Malfunction
problem: The ECU detected an interruption or instability in its power supply circuit.
symptoms: Engine won't start; Erratic idling; Loss of memory settings; Random codes appearing
actions: Check main battery connections for corrosion; Inspect ECU ground points; Test battery voltage (should be 12.6V+); Check main fuse and ignition switch
location: Near the battery or ECU

title: Start Ability Malfunction
problem: The engine is failing to start under normal cranking conditions.
symptoms: Engine cranks but won't start; Delayed starting; Starting only after multiple attempts
actions: Check fuel system pressure; Verify ignition spark presence; Check crankshaft sensor signal; Inspect starter motor circuit
location: Engine bay / starter circuit.

title: Engine RPM Signal Switchover Malfunction
problem: Malfunction in the circuit responsible for switching or processing the engine RPM signal.
symptoms: Engine stalling; Incorrect RPM reading on dash; Starting issues; Rev limiter activating at wrong RPM
actions: Check RPM sensor wiring harness; Inspect ECU connectors for moisture; Verify signal with oscilloscope; Replace crankshaft position sensor
location: Near the flywheel or alternator cover.

title: Inclination Sensor / Immobilizer Communication Error
problem: Error in the inclination (tilt) sensor circuit or ECU-immobilizer communication.
symptoms: Engine cuts out unexpectedly after a fall or tilt; Won't start if bike is tilted; Immobilizer light flashing
actions: Check sensor mounting position (must be upright); Inspect connector for corrosion; Test tilt sensor voltage; Reset tilt sensor by turning ignition off/on
location: Under the seat or near the battery.

title: Crankshaft Position Sensor Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECU is not receiving a valid signal from the CKP sensor on this Honda.
symptoms: Engine won't start; Backfiring; Stalling; No spark condition
actions: Check sensor gap (Honda spec: 0.6–1.0 mm); Inspect sensor wiring harness; Check stator plate condition; Replace CKP sensor
location: Behind the left engine cover near the stator.

title: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor Range/Performance
problem: The MAP sensor reading does not match expected values for the current operating conditions.
symptoms: Hesitation; Poor power; Erratic idle; Rich or lean condition
actions: Check MAP sensor vacuum hose condition; Test MAP sensor at idle vs WOT; Check for intake air leaks; Replace MAP sensor
location: Intake manifold.

title: Catalyst System Efficiency Below Threshold
problem: The catalytic converter is not reducing emissions as effectively as required.
symptoms: Check engine light only; Possible slight fuel smell from exhaust
actions: Check for exhaust leaks before catalytic converter; Inspect O2 sensor operation (upstream and downstream); Check for engine misfires causing catalyst damage; Replace catalytic converter if degraded
location: On the exhaust pipe

title: Vehicle Speed Sensor Malfunction
problem: The ECU is not receiving a valid signal from the speed sensor on this TVS motorcycle.
symptoms: Speedometer not working; Erratic speed display; ABS light on (ABS models)
actions: Check sensor at front/rear wheel; Clean sensor tip and tone ring; Inspect wiring; Replace VSS
location: Rear wheel hub or front fork area.

title: Mass Air Flow Sensor Circuit Low Input
problem: The MAF sensor signal is below the expected minimum value.
symptoms: Rich running condition; Black smoke; Poor throttle response
actions: Check MAF sensor connector; Clean MAF sensor with electronics cleaner (do not touch wire); Test MAF output voltage; Replace MAF sensor
location: In the air intake path

title: Mass Air Flow Sensor Circuit High Input
problem: The MAF sensor signal is above the expected maximum value.
symptoms: Lean condition; Hesitation; Poor fuel economy
actions: Check MAF sensor wiring for short to power; Test sensor at idle; Clean air filter; Replace MAF sensor
location: In the air intake path

title: O2 Sensor Circuit (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
problem: The upstream O2 sensor circuit has a fault — signal missing or incorrect.
symptoms: Poor fuel economy; Rough running; Check engine light; Failed emissions test
actions: Check O2 sensor wiring and connector; Test sensor voltage at operating temperature; Check for exhaust leaks; Replace O2 sensor
location: On the exhaust header pipe.

title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
problem: The internal heater element of the O2 sensor has a circuit fault.
symptoms: Engine takes longer to reach closed-loop; Poor cold-start fuel economy; Check engine light
actions: Test heater circuit resistance (typically 2–30 Ω); Check 12V supply to heater element; Inspect sensor wiring; Replace O2 sensor
location: O2 sensor on exhaust header.

title: Injector Circuit Open — Cylinder 1
problem: The fuel injector circuit for cylinder 1 has an open circuit — no current flow detected.
symptoms: Engine misfire; Won't start or very rough start; Loss of power
actions: Check injector connector and terminal pins; Test injector coil resistance (typically 11–16 Ω); Inspect wiring harness for broken wire; Replace injector if open coil
location: On the intake manifold

title: Ignition Coil 'A' Primary Circuit Malfunction
problem: A fault has been detected in the primary winding circuit of ignition coil A.
symptoms: No spark on cylinder; Engine misfire; Hard starting or no start
actions: Measure coil primary resistance (typically 0.5–3 Ω); Check 12V supply to coil positive terminal; Inspect HT lead and spark plug cap resistance; Replace ignition coil
location: Mounted near the cylinder head.

title: Ignition Coil 'B' Primary Circuit Malfunction
problem: A fault has been detected in the primary winding circuit of ignition coil B (twin-cylinder models).
symptoms: Misfire on second cylinder; Rough running; Loss of power
actions: Measure coil B primary resistance; Swap coil A and B to see if fault follows; Check ECU coil driver output; Replace ignition coil B
location: Mounted near the second cylinder head.

title: Camshaft Position Sensor Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECU is not receiving a signal from the CMP sensor on this Suzuki.
symptoms: Hard starting; Engine stalling; Timing-related poor performance
actions: Check CMP sensor wiring and connector; Test sensor at operating temperature; Inspect target wheel (cam trigger); Replace CMP sensor
location: Near the valve cover / cam end.

title: System Voltage Low
problem: Battery voltage has dropped below the threshold required for safe ECU operation on this Kawasaki.
symptoms: Electrical systems failing; ECU faults triggering; Dim lights; Poor starting
actions: Test battery – should be 12.6V+ at rest
location: 13.5–14.5V running; Check charging system (stator and regulator/rectifier); Inspect main ground lead to engine; Replace battery or regulator if faulty

title: Throttle Position Sensor Circuit Low Voltage
problem: TPS voltage is below expected minimum on this Hero model.
symptoms: Stalling at idle; Poor acceleration; Engine hunting
actions: Check TPS connector for moisture; Verify 5V reference supply; Adjust TPS if adjustable; Replace TPS
location: Side of throttle body.
